Answer: A
Reason: Figure 1a shows a large right pleural effusion (fluid in the lower hemithorax) associated with a mediastinal abscess containing air (arrow), which is significantly larger than the small left-sided collection seen in Figure 1b. This constellation of findings—a mediastinal infection/abscess and a dominant right pleural effusion—is highly characteristic of an aorto-oesophageal fistula, where the effusion is secondary to the mediastinal pathology.
